content.overview: Section 105 regulates appointment and use of proxies at company meetings. It addresses eligibility to appoint a proxy, limits on speaking and voting, notice disclosures, deposit timing, instrument formalities, prescribed forms and inspection of lodged proxies. Applicable rules and company articles must also be checked.
content.glance: A member entitled to attend and vote may generally appoint a proxy subject to section 105, applicable rules and the company's articles. A proxy has no right to speak and may vote only on a poll; the section also regulates notice statements, instrument formalities, deposit and inspection.
content.study:
## Statutory framework
Section 105(1) permits a member entitled to attend and vote at a company meeting to appoint another person as proxy, subject to its provisos. The section states that a proxy cannot speak at the meeting and cannot vote except on a poll. It also addresses companies without share capital, classes of companies that may be prescribed as restricted, and the prescribed cap on the number of members and shares represented.

Section 105(2) requires a prominent proxy-entitlement statement in the specified meeting notices and clarifies that the proxy need not be a member. The remaining subsections address consequences for default, a 48-hour ceiling for advance deposit requirements, company-funded invitations to appoint specified proxies, writing and signature requirements for the instrument, prescribed form protection, and inspection of proxies lodged subject to the stated notice and timing conditions.

## Application checklist
Identify whether the member is entitled to attend and vote; check the company's articles and applicable rules; inspect the notice statement; verify the proxy instrument, signature and prescribed form; check deposit timing; and distinguish attendance from speaking and voting rights. Do not treat this summary as a substitute for the complete current section and rules.

## Verification limit
The official India Code Act PDF is linked as the source for section 105. A section-specific India Code deep link was not established for this topic. Amendment history, applicable rules, company-specific exemptions and section-specific case law remain open for verification.

sections.heading: Eligibility and appointment
sections.body: Section 105(1) addresses appointment by a member entitled to attend and vote at the meeting. Apply the statutory provisos and check applicable rules and the company's articles before concluding that a particular appointment is permitted.

sections.heading: Speaking and voting limits
sections.body: The proviso to section 105(1) states that a proxy has no right to speak at the meeting and is not entitled to vote except on a poll. Do not equate the proxy's attendance with the member's full participation rights.

sections.heading: Notice and instrument requirements
sections.body: Section 105(2) requires the specified notice of meeting to state with reasonable prominence that an entitled member may appoint a proxy and that the proxy need not be a member. Section 105(6) requires the instrument to be in writing and signed by the appointer or a duly authorised person, with the body-corporate requirements stated in the section.

sections.heading: Deposit, prescribed form and inspection
sections.body: Section 105(4) limits provisions requiring deposit more than 48 hours before the meeting by treating the permitted period as 48 hours. Section 105(7) addresses instruments in the prescribed form. Section 105(8) provides an inspection right during the specified 24-hour period before commencement through conclusion, subject to at least three days' written notice and business-hour conditions.

sections.heading: Compliance and current-law check
sections.body: The section contains separate consequences for specified defaults and company-funded invitations to appoint named proxies. Confirm the currently operative penalty wording, prescribed classes, prescribed number/share limits and rules against official current sources before advising.

examples.title: Proxy appointed for a member
examples.body: A member entitled to attend and vote appoints a proxy using an instrument that meets the statutory and prescribed formalities. The proxy's participation remains limited by section 105 and applicable rules; appointment alone does not confer a right to speak.

examples.title: Proxy attempts to speak or vote other than on a poll
examples.body: A proxy attempts to address the meeting and cast a vote by show of hands. Section 105's proviso states that a proxy has no right to speak and may vote only on a poll; apply the complete current Act and relevant rules to the meeting record.

hypotheticals.question: A member appoints a proxy, who then attempts to speak and vote by show of hands. What does section 105 provide?
hypotheticals.analysis: The proviso to section 105(1) denies a proxy the right to speak and provides that the proxy is not entitled to vote except on a poll. Check whether the member was entitled to attend and vote, whether the instrument complies with the Act and rules, and whether any applicable statutory exception changes the result.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming a proxy may speak because the proxy may attend.
misconceptions.correction: The proviso to section 105(1) says a proxy has no right to speak at the meeting.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming a proxy may vote in every voting mode.
misconceptions.correction: Section 105 states that the proxy is not entitled to vote except on a poll.

misconceptions.trap: Treating proxy appointment as a purely informal act.
misconceptions.correction: Check writing, signature, prescribed form, deposit timing, notice disclosure, inspection requirements and the applicable rules.

questionsAndAnswers.answer: Section 105 addresses eligibility to appoint a proxy, limits on speaking and voting, notice disclosure, proxy instrument formalities, deposit timing, prescribed forms and inspection of lodged proxies. The full section, applicable rules and articles must be checked for the specific meeting.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should be checked when a proxy appointment is challenged?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Verify the member's entitlement to attend and vote, the appointment instrument and signature, prescribed form, deposit deadline, notice statement, inspection conditions, relevant rules and company articles. Do not assume the proxy may speak or vote other than on a poll. Section-specific case law has not been independently verified for this topic.
